leading_positions.synthesis: Three of eight members (Aili, Chabes, Linke) prefer targeted protein degradation as a single-part prize, and all three name the same laureates: Crews, Deshaies and Handa. They share the view that PROTACs (Crews, Deshaies) and the cereblon mechanism of molecular glues (Handa) form one induced-proximity idea, and that the mechanism is chemically explicit and independently reproduced. They differ in emphasis and citation wording: Aili's citation spans PROTAC design through the cereblon-mediated molecular-glue mechanism, while Chabes and Linke word it around small molecules directing the ubiquitin-proteasome system. They also differ in what they would change: Aili would put Handa ahead of Ciulli in a three-person cut, Linke asks whether Deshaies, Ciulli or Ito should displace one name, and Chabes questions the omission of Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto. All three concede that no degrader is yet approved. B063 is named as an alternative by Brzezinski, Somfai, Sparr and Zou, but those four do not prefer it.

Two members prefer ionizable lipid nanoparticles, as the carrier counterpart to the mRNA cargo recognised in 2023 Medicine, with strong maturity and impact. They disagree on the laureates. Sparr proposes Cullis, Hope and Madden, anchored in lipid self-assembly and the Vancouver group. Aqvist proposes Cullis and Anderson. Aqvist also pairs B035 with B068 (base editing, Liu alone) in a two-part prize, so only Aqvist backs both ballots. Sparr's configuration is B035 alone.

One member prefers proton-coupled electron transfer (Mayer, Hammes-Schiffer, Nocera) as a unifying physical principle with an experiment-plus-theory structure. It is a single-member position that the proposer himself flags as near his own field, and the exclusion of T. J. Meyer is acknowledged as unresolved.

One member prefers palladium-catalysed C-N coupling (Hartwig, Buchwald), arguing it is mature and cleanly attributed. The open point is whether it is distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize and how Kosugi and Migita should be treated.

One member prefers rational design of molecular-sieve catalysts (Corma, Davis, Zones), citing maturity and industrial reach. The proposer notes that nobody else ranked it first, that attribution among five candidates is subjective, and that the 2025 framework-materials prize may be seen as an overlap.

Base editing (Liu alone) appears in round 1 only as the second part of Aqvist's two-part configuration. Aqvist has moved from prime editing (B061) in the opening to base editing, now listing B061 as an alternative. Aili and Chabes list B068 as an alternative but do not prefer it.

areas_of_agreement: Every member's round-1 statement treats targeted protein degradation (B063) as a serious candidate: three prefer it and four more (Brzezinski, Somfai, Sparr, Zou) list it as an alternative. Aqvist places it among the alternatives as well, so all eight files mention it. Whether this reflects merit or just breadth of support is itself contested.
The three members who prefer B063 name the same laureate set (Crews, Deshaies, Handa), so the first-ranked proposal is not split on names.

Members broadly agree that independent reproduction and demonstrated chemical content matter, and that candidates differ in how well they meet that standard rather than in whether the standard applies.
No member recommends recusal. Every member describes any proximity to a candidate as a bias to be weighed, not a disqualifying tie.
Members consistently note that every candidate at least partly excludes someone with a substantive claim, so attribution is a shared difficulty and not a point on which one candidate stands apart.
scientific_disputes: Whether several candidates are chemistry or medicine and pharmaceutical technology: the lipid nanoparticle and base-editing proposals (B035, B068) are challenged on this ground by their own proposers, Sparr and Aqvist.
Whether PROTAC design and the cereblon/molecular-glue mechanism are one discovery or two historically distinct achievements, raised by Aili, Chabes and Linke.
Whether proton-coupled electron transfer (B025) is a single discovery or a broad field, as Brzezinski himself flags.

Whether palladium C-N coupling (B032) is a new discovery or an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and whether molecular-sieve design (B051) is sufficiently distinct from the 2025 framework-materials prize.

Whether breadth of opening support (all eight members included B063) is evidence of merit or a poor proxy for it. Chabes weighs it heavily; Aili and Linke caution that it does not by itself prove merit.
attribution_disputes: B063: Crews, Deshaies and Handa are named by all three supporters, but Ciulli (VHL ligands), Ito (cereblon co-discoverer), Gray, Sakamoto and Kim are each cited as having a claim. Aili would favour Handa over Ciulli; Linke asks whether Deshaies, Ciulli or Ito should displace one of the three; Chabes questions the omission of Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto.

B035: the two supporters disagree on laureates (Cullis, Hope, Madden versus Cullis and Anderson). Anderson, Langer, MacLachlan and Madden/Hope are each cited as having claims, and patent disputes complicate the record.
B068: a Liu-only citation leaves out Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo, and B061 (Anzalone) is the alternative genome-editing choice.
B025: T. J. Meyer's foundational work against the three-person limit; B032: the Kosugi and Migita precedent; B051: which three of Corma, Davis, Zones, Yu and Tsapatsis.
maturity_disputes: B063: no degrader is yet approved, and Aili, Chabes and Linke each name this as the main reservation. They differ on whether it is disqualifying now or merely a reason to wait. Chabes asks what clinical milestones would suffice, and Sparr and Zou ask whether an approval would shift the ordering.
B068 is under a decade old with long-term safety not established. Aqvist treats it as better matured than prime editing (B061), while Aili raises the same maturity concern against prime editing.

B032 and B051 are mature, with 25 or more years of reproduction. Their proposers Somfai and Zou consider the maturity question settled, so for these candidates the dispute is overlap with earlier prizes and not timing.
B035 is mature in impact (siRNA drugs and billions of vaccine doses); the dispute is whether the 2023 Medicine prize already covered the territory.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Brzezinski: his research on proton transfer in respiratory enzymes is scientifically close to B025, which he prefers; he asks colleagues to weigh his enthusiasm accordingly but sees no recusal as necessary.

Zou: his research on electron crystallography of zeolites is close to B051, which he prefers; he asks whether this proximity warrants recusal on that ballot. He is also a Stockholm University colleague of Brzezinski, which he says does not bear on a candidate.
Sparr: her research on lipid self-assembly and membrane biophysics is close to B035 and B046; she has no stated tie to any credited candidate and will declare any later association.
Somfai: synthetic organic methodology is his field, which he flags as a field bias toward B032; no tie to any candidate.
Chabes: biochemistry and medical chemistry background, flagged as a possible bias toward chemical-biology candidates.
Aqvist: postdoctoral mentor Warshel is not named on any shortlisted ballot; computational interest touches B025 only at the field level, not seen as a recusal issue.
Linke (chair): no candidate tie. A shared Lund affiliation with Somfai and Sparr is among members, not with a candidate. Aili reports no flag.
questions_for_round2: Is the absence of an approved degrader disqualifying for B063 this year, and if not, what evidence of clinical or mechanistic validation would the committee accept as sufficient?

Should the B063 citation cover PROTAC design and the cereblon/glue mechanism together, or be narrowed to one strand, and who holds the three places: Handa, Deshaies or Ciulli, with Ito, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim?

If B035 is the alternative to B063, can its attribution be settled (Cullis with Hope and Madden, or with Anderson), and does the committee treat ionizable lipid nanoparticles as chemistry rather than pharmaceutical technology after the 2023 Medicine prize?

Should the committee prefer a single-part prize, or a two-part prize such as the B035 with B068 configuration, and would any single-member candidate (B025, B032, B051) be considered in a multi-part prize?

For B032 and B051, do members see enough distance from the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the 2025 framework-materials prize, and does the committee need a ruling on whether proposers close to their own fields (B025, B051) should abstain on those ballots?
How should breadth of ranking across members be weighed against scientific merit of candidates preferred by one member only, such as B025, B032 and B051?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 yields one plurality position, B063 with three explicit supporters who agree on the same three names, then B035 with two supporters who disagree on names, and three single-member positions (B025, B032, B051). No position reaches the five-member majority. The B063 debate turns on timing and on the third name, and the B035 debate on attribution and whether it counts as chemistry. Neither of these is yet resolved by the round-1 files. Breadth of opening support has been invoked by several members and should not by itself be treated as merit.
